key_insight: Q-Capsule reduces barren-plateau risk by localizing each capsule’s observables and entanglement so gradients stay usable as circuit width grows.
engineering_relevance: The architecture offers a practical design pattern for trainable quantum neural networks that are more scalable, noise-tolerant, and measurement-efficient.
method: Partition the register into localized capsules with mostly local readout.
Use sparse inter-capsule coupling plus trainable data re-uploading to preserve communication.
Grow depth adaptively using QFIM-guided policy instead of fixing a deep global circuit.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports stable gradient variance with increasing width, a log-gradient-variance slope near -ln 2 per qubit for global baselines, and adaptive-policy accuracy of 98.1% on binary and 97.7% on four-class classification.
watch_item: Performance may depend on careful capsule partitioning and QFIM-based depth control, which could add tuning overhead and hardware/compiler complexity.
paper_title: Q-Capsule: A Localized Capsule-Based Quantum Neural Architecture for Barren Plateau Mitigation
